lowest_kept_score.note: Several kept places score 0 views and 0 counted sources on the script's count (their counted sources were found by the judge on re-look), so every left-out candidate with any views or a counted source is listed below with its reason.

stronger_left_out.name: Cape Leeuwin
stronger_left_out.reason: Wikivoyage Margaret River 'See' names Cape Leeuwin; margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) 'Edge of the world: the great Cape Leeuwin' (where two oceans meet, whales). Strong name (16k views). Skeptic: Not a separate place from Cape Leeuwin Lighthouse: visitors reach the cape at the lighthouse precinct (ticketed grounds, interpretive centre), which is listed separately by Wikivoyage and the board. Keep as ONE spot (the lighthouse, with 'where two oceans meet' in its bio) rather than both; review only to decide which name carries it.

stronger_left_out.name: Busselton Underwater Observatory
stronger_left_out.reason: Rule 3: part of a larger spot. It is at the end of Busselton Jetty and is sold as part of the jetty visit (Wikivoyage Busselton lists it under the jetty); Busselton Jetty is kept and its bio covers the observatory.

stronger_left_out.name: Margaret River wine region
stronger_left_out.reason: Duplicate of Margaret River: Wikivoyage says 'Margaret River is now the common term for the region between the capes'; kept as one under the Margaret River candidate (proposer decides whether the destination is the town or the region).

stronger_left_out.name: Cape Naturaliste
stronger_left_out.reason: Wikivoyage Leeuwin-Naturaliste NP and margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) 'Cape Naturaliste' scenic-spot page (boardwalks, Whale Lookout walk, Cape Naturaliste loop, track to Sugarloaf Rock). Skeptic: Shares its car park and precinct with Cape Naturaliste Lighthouse, listed separately; the walks are short sections of the Cape to Cape Track. Keep as one with the lighthouse unless the owner wants the headland walks as their own spot.

stronger_left_out.name: Northcliffe
stronger_left_out.reason: Re-looked: southernforestsandvalleys.com (Southern Forests & Valleys regional tourism) town page and itinerary name the Understory Art & Nature Walk, the Pioneer Museum, Mount Chudalup and Windy Harbour nearby. Skeptic: For: gateway to D'Entrecasteaux NP and Windy Harbour with a named art trail and museum. Against: one counted source, and its named draws (Understory, Mount Chudalup) are separate candidates, so the town may be a wrapper.

stronger_left_out.name: Boyup Brook
stronger_left_out.reason: Re-looked: only southernforestsandvalleys.com (Southern Forests & Valleys regional tourism) lists it, with generic text ('natural wonders, local artisans, local produce'); no named sight. Skeptic: Against: one counted source and nothing specific to see or do (brief: a town with nothing a source names is reject or review). For: a listed town of the regional board, gateway for country-music events (events do not count).

stronger_left_out.name: Lake Clifton
stronger_left_out.reason: Outside the region: belongs to wa-perth (the lake and its thrombolite boardwalk are in the Peel / Yalgorup National Park area; wa-perth's candidate list already has 'Lake Clifton Thrombolites').

stronger_left_out.name: Prevelly
stronger_left_out.reason: Re-looked: margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) 'Prevelly & Gnarabup' town page names the beaches, Margaret River Mouth, St John the Theologian Church, the Prevelly Sculpture Loop Walk and Surfers Point. Skeptic: Against: its headline draw is Surfers Point (kept separately), so the village is likely a wrapper or near-duplicate (COVERAGE: never list a town beside its own attraction). For: a named surf village with its own beaches and river mouth.

stronger_left_out.name: Diamond Tree
stronger_left_out.reason: Rule 2: DBCA says the Diamond Tree is 'now permanently CLOSED for climbing' (rot in the base, 2019); what is left is a picnic area and short walk at a roadside tree. Its draw (climbing) is closed and Wikivoyage's listing is out of date.

stronger_left_out.name: Australind
stronger_left_out.reason: Re-looked: harveyregion.com.au (Shire of Harvey tourism) Australind page names the Australind Jetty, the Leschenault Waterways Eco Museum, the estuary crabbing and the heritage trail. Skeptic: Against: one local-government tourism source; a residential satellite of Bunbury ('Australia's fastest growing regional location') with cafes and a big pub; a traveller from elsewhere rarely goes out of their way for it. For: estuary jetty and eco museum.

stronger_left_out.name: Moondyne Cave
stronger_left_out.reason: Rule 2 / brief (closed places are rejected): Wikipedia says Moondyne Cave is not currently open for tours; Wikivoyage lists the name with no details, and neither margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) nor DBCA offers it.

Skeptic: For: two counted sources, a pioneer estate. Against: a cellar door and restaurant like many others; the brief keeps a winery only when singled out as a destination.

stronger_left_out.reason: Board listing (australiassouthwest.com) and margaretriver.com (Margaret River Busselton Tourism Association, the regional board) winery page: founding winery (1970), twice Jimmy Watson trophy winner, cellar door daily, vineyard tours. Skeptic: For: a founding estate a board names. Against: a cellar door like dozens of others, with no visitor attraction beyond tasting; the brief keeps a winery only when singled out as a destination in its own right.

benchmark.note: COVERAGE step 6's benchmarks are New Zealand places and do not apply to this Western Australia region. Region checks instead: Busselton Jetty, Cape Leeuwin Lighthouse, the Leeuwin-Naturaliste caves (Ngilgi, Jewel, Lake, Mammoth, Calgardup, Giants), Gloucester Tree, Dave Evans Bicentennial Tree, the Cape to Cape Track and the Dolphin Discovery Centre are all kept and placed; operators and vehicles (Pemberton Tramway, Whale Watch WA, cruise and tour operators) are rejected in favour of the places; once-a-week markets and events (Puzzletown6255, the Southern Art & Craft Trail, the Blues at Bridgetown festival) are rejected; gateway villages whose draw lies beyond them (Northcliffe, Prevelly, Boyup Brook) went to review, not keep.
